normal.notes:
Connecting from your iPhone is much faster. A connection could take 30–40 seconds even on a perfect network: while your iPhone waited for this Mac's reply it asked again, and this Mac took each repeat as a brand-new viewer and threw away the reply it had already sent. It now answers the same question once and keeps it. This Mac also notices straight away when your iPhone leaves, and reconnects by itself after sleep or a Wi-Fi change, so it is ready the moment you connect again.

No more mouse lag at the start of a session. The first few seconds used to send two full-screen pictures back to back at full quality, so the pointer ran seconds behind your finger. Now one picture is sent, quality ramps up over the first three seconds, and your clicks and moves no longer wait behind other start-up work.

Also: a safety fix — a second device that connects while you're in a session now always has to enter the password before it can see or control this Mac.

beta.notes:
Connect: viewer re-offers re-send the same localDescription; the host dedupes a repeat offer by a=ice-ufrag and re-sends its answer instead of resetForNewViewer (which orphaned answer #1 and wedged the viewer until the 45s UI deadline). Stale-pc guards on every SDP hop; remoteDescriptionSet only on a successful setRemote. Candidates arriving with pc == nil are buffered; the viewer re-trickles all local candidates once the answer applies. Idle host rebuilds its pc on re-welcome (fresh TURN creds). Control-channel .closed ends the session immediately (was 12–18s). Signaling: WS ping with a 10s pong deadline, send errors and wake/NWPath changes force a reconnect. Release os.Logger category "connect" logs each phase in ms.

Lag: viewer keyframe requests coalesced within 1.5s of a forced IDR (no double IDR at auth); 3s start ramp at ≤3 Mbps / 1× data cap that survives setQuality; input injected on a dedicated serial queue under an identity+epoch-checked lock, resetButtons ordered after accepted input.

Security: authorization is keyed on a per-pc peer epoch, so a pc rebuilt inside the reused online WebRTCConnection can't inherit the previous viewer's input/video grant; stale channels, auth replies and challenges are dropped.
